primitive.relation: Attained hypergraph Ramsey number: hg_ramsey_number E C R holds when the host I_R forces a monochromatic copy of the pattern E : {set {set T}} under the palette C : Type (D5 hg_forces_mono) and every forcing host size N has R <= N. R is supplied: no existence theorem, choice or minimum extraction; arbitrary carrier, family and palette, no uniformity, nonempty-family, inhabited-palette or positivity guard (empty palette: minimum 0; a colour and the empty family: minimum #|T|). The Extremal graph-arrow Ramsey numbers (X195, X215) are separate interfaces.

hypergraph-attained-forcing-minimum.note: x117_ramsey_number t R is hg_ramsey_number (x117_edges t) bool R and x119_ramsey_number E q R is hg_ramsey_number E I_q R: forcing at R and minimality over the D5 forcing view, same carrier, family and palette, headers and implicit arguments unchanged.

graph-family-arrow-minimum.note: x195_ramsey_number k r Fam n: K_n arrows the finite family of simple graphs in k colours and no smaller K_m does. A graph-arrow interface, deferred to a later graph-Ramsey class of this owner; not claimed inequivalent; source, arrows and rows untouched.

diagonal-clique-arrow-minimum.note: x215_ramsey_number k N: the Boolean diagonal clique arrow holds at N and fails below. A graph-arrow interface (with the existing X215/X195 bridge), deferred to a later graph-Ramsey class; the blocked rational-limit row and the source are untouched.

upstream_audit.note: No Ramsey-number contract upstream; MathComp ex_minn extracts a witness from an existence proof and is not this supplied-R Prop. The canonical reuses the D5 forcing view with nat inequalities; no second-area consumer, so it stays in Hypergraph.
